title: experiment-exposure-heuristics-and-slice-simulation-notes
body:
Context and intent:
This is a working notes doc for refining cross-functional heuristics used to decide exposure slices and rollback thresholds for canaries and A/B experiments. Focus is on practical, testable rules that product, SRE, and solutions engineers can apply without heavy instrumentation changes.

High-level goals:
- Reduce time-to-decision for early-stage traffic experiments (canaries) while keeping user and cost risk bounded.
- Prioritize signals that matter for end-user experience (latency tail, generation correctness flags) and for economics (per-token cost deltas).
- Make gating rules auditable and easy to communicate to PMs/Eng/CS.

Assumptions and constraints (notes to self):
- We must assume heterogeneous client behavior; some slices generate long sequences heavily benefiting from KV cache, others short queries.
- Not every customer has the full observability (token-level breakdown) enabled; heuristics need fallbacks that use simpler metrics (p99 latency, error-rate).
- For private deployments, rollback timelines may be longer due to change windows. Account for deployment-class in allocation policy.

Proposed exposure heuristic (first cut):
1) Warmed micro-canary (0.1% traffic, 1 hour):
   - Purpose: validate runtime compatibility, detect immediate regressions (errors, OOMs).
   - Hard abort if: total error rate > 1.0% absolute increase vs baseline OR any OOM/instance-crash.
   - Soft hold if: p99 latency increases by > 2x (investigate for 30m).

2) Functional canary (1% traffic, 4 hours):
   - Purpose: surface quality regressions (LLM hallucinations, regression on prompt set) and cost/latency signals at scale.
   - Commit criteria: no catastrophic errors, automated regression eval (sampled prompts) passes with delta < 3% relative to baseline on primary eval metric; per-token cost delta < 10% of baseline.
   - Abort criteria: eval fail OR sustained error-rate increase > 0.5% for 60m OR p95 latency increase > 25% for 30m.

3) Exposure ramp (5% -> 20% -> 50% over 24-72h):
   - Each step requires a short steady-state window (2x median request duration or 1h min).
   - At each step, run A/B comparisons on key metrics (engagement, CTR where applicable, conversion proxy). Use sequential testing but enforce minimum sample sizes to avoid premature conclusions.

Traffic-slice selection heuristics:
- Start with low-variance cohorts: internal-traffic, beta users, high-traffic customers with simple requests (to validate stability).
- Avoid slices dominated by long-tail sequences during early ramps (they skew cost and latency).
- Prioritize geographic slices only after functional canary passes (reduce geo-driven noise early).
- If testing model variants tuned for specific workloads, route matching-profile users first (e.g., embeddings-heavy customers to embedding-optimized variant).

Signal prioritization (ranking for decisioning):
1) Safety-critical failures (crash, data loss, security alerts) — immediate abort.
2) Silent functional regressions detected by automated evals (precision/recall for rerank, toxicity increase) — high-priority.
3) Error rate deltas (5xx/timeout) — medium priority with short windows.
4) Latency tail increases (p95/p99) — medium/low depending on absolute magnitude and business tolerance.
5) Cost per request token delta — low priority for short canaries, higher for sustained exposure.

Abort decision tree (operational flow):
- T0: alert fires (metric X exceeds threshold) -> Pager to on-call SRE and product lead (same page).
- T+5m: on-call validates noise or real signal via logs and traces.
- T+15m: if validated and matches abort criteria -> trigger immediate route reversion to baseline (automated) + start incident postmortem.
- If ambiguous, escalate to cross-functional war room and hold further ramping until resolved.

Quick checklist for rollout playbook page (copy into console runbook):
- [ ] Canary config committed (traffic percentages, duration)
- [ ] Experiment sampling code reviewed (seeded randomization checked)
- [ ] Relevant dashboards linked (latency, errors, cost, evals)
- [ ] Stakeholders notified (PM, Eng, SRE, CS)
- [ ] Communication template prepared (customer-facing if needed)
- [ ] Rollback script verified and tested in staging

Simulation experiments (notes from a quick local run):
- Ran synthetic traffic for two user profiles: short-query (avg len 12 tokens) and long-query (avg len 420 tokens).
- When mixing in 10% long-query traffic during a 1% canary, p99 jumped by 3.1x despite overall request rate being low — conclusion: don't mix long-tail-heavy slices early.
- Cost impact simulation: switching to quantized model variant reduced per-token CPU by 18% but increased p95 latency by 12% under bursty loads; suggests need for hybrid routing by SLA (low-latency customers -> non-quantized).

Open questions and tradeoffs (action items):
- How do we encode cost sensitivity into automated abort thresholds without creating noise for low-value traffic? (action: Diego to draft cost weighting heuristic, due 2025-01-20)
- Should we add a tiered delay for rollback in private/on-prem deployments? Need legal/customer ops input on change windows. (action: Rina to check customer agreements)
- When do we prefer A/B over canary? For feature-driven UX metrics prefer A/B to get product signals; for infra/runtime changes prefer canaries. Need explicit checklist to decide. (action: Liam to draft decision table)
- Are our eval corpora representative for the slices we test? We observed several mismatches for enterprise-heavy prompts. (action: Sana to create representative seed sets per customer cohort)

Cross-functional responsibilities (practical breakdown):
- Product: defines success metric and primary evaluation prompts, communicates stakeholders, signs off on ramp steps.
- SRE: sets hard abort thresholds (crash/OOM/etc), owns rollback automation and monitoring hooks.
- Solutions Eng / CS: identifies customer cohorts for early exposure and flags any VIP constraints.
- Data/ML (Applied ML): builds automated evals for quality regressions and tracks relative model score deltas.

Communication templates (short):
- Internal incident note snippet: "Canary v2.3.1->v2.3.2 observed p99 latency +210% in slice X; automated rollback executed at 14:22 UTC. Investigating root cause; postmortem will be posted to CONFLUENCE-ID within 48h."
- Customer-facing blurb: "We detected an operational anomaly associated with a new model rollout and reverted the change to protect performance for your workloads. Our team is investigating; we'll follow up with details and remediation plan."

Quick experiments to run next quarter (proposals):
- A/B with exposure-weighted sampling: bias towards low-cost requests in early ramps to reduce cost noise. Measure detection power for quality regressions.
- Synthetic workload replay from prod traces to estimate cost-latency sensitivity by cohort.
- Ramp policy variant test: aggressive (fast 1%->20% in 12h) vs conservative (staggered 5% steps over 72h) and see which converges faster without false-aborts.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally prescriptive but still rough — want feedback on thresholds and whether the prioritization map matches SRE/business tolerances. If agreed, next step is turning the checklist into a template in the Console runbook UI and implementing simple gating in the rollout orchestration service.

Recent edits (log):
- 2025-01-12: added simulation experiment results and revised p99 early-warning threshold guidance.
- 2025-01-27: inserted abort decision tree and expanded cross-functional roles.
- 2025-02-03: added action items and communication templates.
